newsitem.title: USA: Cyberonics to focus on FDA approval.
newsitem.headline: Cyberonics to focus on FDA approval.

text.p: Cyberonics Inc said on Thursday it would focus on gaining U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of its lead product following St. Jude Medical Inc's decision not to complete a proposed $72 million acquisition of the company.
On Wednesday St. Jude said it would not exercise its option to acquire all the oustanding shares of Cyberonics.
In the next 18 to 24 months Cyberonics will focus on getting its NeuroCybernetic Prosthesis System through the FDA, the company said.
It plans to expand its sales and marketing activities for the system in international markets where it is approved for sale, it said.
The company's device stimulates the vagus nerve in the neck and reduces the incidence of seizure in patients with epilepsy and other neurological disorders.

As part of the nixed merger plan, which was first announced in April, St. Jude made a $12 million equity investment in Cyberonics. St. Jude said on Thursday it will maintain its equity position in Cyberonics.
The investment was aimed at providing Cyberonics with funding through the FDA approval process in the event that St. Jude decided not to go forward with the acquisition, Cyberonics said.
Cyberonics said it was told by St. Jude that it cancelled the deal for "strategic reasons."

St. Jude chief executive Ronald Matricaria declined to comment in an interview Wednesday on analysts' speculation that St. Jude found problems with data from medical trials testing Texas-based Cyberonics' device.
He said the company would not rule out possibly someday acquiring Cyberonics.
